## Ecological Background

The Asian long-horned beetle (*Anoplophora glabripennis*, ALB) is a wood-boring insect native to China and Korea that attacks the stems of multiple deciduous tree species and spreads internationally via wood packaging material (Haack et al., 1997; Eyre & Haack, 2017).

While direct tree mortality in non-urban forest stands can be gradual on hosts with dbh ≥ 7.5 cm (Dodds & Orwig, 2011), eradication measures upon detection typically dominate stand-level tree removals (Nowak et al., 2001; Faccoli & Gatto, 2016).

## Model Implementation

ALB uses a leptokurtic dispersal kernel (`exp(-0.1478*sqrt(x))`, `maxDistance: 1000` m; Smith et al., 2001; Shatz et al., 2016) and colonizes 10 m cells containing Sycamore maple (`acps`) with dbh ≥ 7.5 cm. Without detailed population-dynamics data, `BiteBiomass` is omitted and annual mortality increases linearly from 0 to 2% over 10 years.

To represent management eradication responses, `onSetup` loads a stand ID grid (`standId`), and `BiteImpact.onImpact` accumulates damage per stand via `ABELink()`. Once accumulated impact exceeds the detection threshold (3 years), `fmengine.runActivity(standId, 'disturbance_response')` triggers an [ABE](../../../wiki/abe.qmd) harvest activity across that stand.
